summary: Lunar Horizon is an interactive decision-support tool designed to help users compare potential lunar landing sites and landing dates, with a focus on the Moon's south pole. It visualizes the positions of the Sun and Earth relative to a selected lunar location and time, helping users evaluate solar illumination opportunities and direct-to-Earth communication windows. By combining NASA's JPL Horizons ephemeris data with lunar surface and illumination datasets, the tool aims to translate complex astronomical information into clear, comparable operational indicators. Its purpose is to make lunar landing scenario assessment more accessible, supporting mission planning, engineering coordination, education, and public understanding of the challenges of lunar exploration.
details:
Lunar Horizon is designed as a web-based lunar landing scenario comparison tool focused on two critical operational constraints: solar illumination and direct-to-Earth communication.

Users can select candidate lunar landing locations and dates to examine the apparent positions of the Sun and Earth relative to the local horizon. The interface organizes this information into visual indicators, including solar elevation, sunlight availability, Earth visibility, and communication windows.

The proposed data workflow combines NASA/JPL Horizons ephemerides with lunar surface and illumination information from NASA's Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) datasets. These resources provide the scientific basis for evaluating celestial geometry and understanding how lunar terrain can affect visibility.

The main innovation is the integration of information that is normally distributed across specialized scientific tools into a single, accessible comparison experience. Instead of requiring users to navigate multiple technical interfaces, Lunar Horizon presents landing scenarios in a consistent format to support faster assessment.

The initial scope prioritizes a focused comparison of selected landing sites and dates. Terrain-dependent horizon calculations will be included only where the available elevation data and implementation permit reliable results.

The tool is intended for educational and preliminary mission-planning purposes. Its outputs are not certified flight-planning predictions, and geometric visibility must not be confused with guaranteed electrical power generation or an operational communication link.
